title: ACID Atomicity vs Consistency #1
statement: Which component of an RDBMS is primarily responsible for ensuring Atomicity during transaction failures?
explanation: The Recovery Manager uses undo logs from WAL to rollback incomplete transaction state on abort/crash.

title: Lossless Join Decomposition #2
statement: A decomposition of relation R into R1 and R2 is lossless if and only if (R1 ∩ R2) functionally determines:

options.text: Either R1 or R2 (i.e. (R1 ∩ R2) is a superkey of R1 or R2)

explanation: Lossless join condition requires the shared intersection attribute (R1 ∩ R2) to be a superkey of at least one of the decomposed tables.

title: Two-Phase Locking (2PL) Protocol #3
statement: What does Strict Two-Phase Locking (Strict 2PL) guarantee that basic 2PL does not?

options.text: Strict 2PL prevents cascading rollbacks by holding exclusive locks until transaction commit

explanation: Strict 2PL holds exclusive locks until COMMIT/ABORT, preventing dirty reads and cascading aborts.

title: Clustered vs Non-Clustered Index #4
statement: How many Clustered Indexes can exist on a single database table in standard RDBMS like PostgreSQL or MySQL?

options.text: Equal to the number of columns
Exactly 1, because the physical ordering of data rows on disk is unique

explanation: A clustered index determines the physical storage layout of data rows on disk, so only one can exist per table.
